intro: Oslo rewards visitors with a mix of culture, nature, and Scandinavian cool. Pick how long you have and what you enjoy most.
tour_note: Check the tour page for which entry tickets are included.

notes: Metro (T-bane), trams, and buses cover the city; use the Ruter app or buy tickets at kiosks.
Ride apps Uber and Bolt operate in Oslo.
Taxis are expensive; Oslo Taxi and NorgesTaxi are reliable.
Driving is not recommended due to tolls and limited parking.
Walking and biking are easy in the compact centre; bike-sharing available.
Ferries connect to Bygdøy museums and islands in the fjord.

vigeland.name: Vigeland Park
vigeland.price_text: Free park entry · Vigeland Museum separate fee
vigeland.hours: Park open 24 hours · museum Tue–Sun, check on the day
vigeland.tip: Go early morning to see the sculptures without crowds. The Monolith is at the highest point of the park.

akershus.name: Akershus Fortress
akershus.price_text: Free grounds · castle interior has a fee, check on the day
akershus.hours: Grounds open daily, roughly 06:00–21:00 · interiors shorter hours
akershus.tip: Walk the ramparts for harbour views, then head down to Aker Brygge for lunch.

opera.name: Oslo Opera House
opera.price_text: Free to walk the roof · performance tickets vary
opera.hours: Foyer roughly 10:00–18:00 · roof open longer in summer
opera.tip: Walk up the sloping marble roof for a free view over the fjord. Wear shoes with grip.

vikingship.name: Viking Ship Museum, Oslo
vikingship.price_text: Check on the day — the museum has been closed for rebuilding
vikingship.hours: Check on the day before you go
vikingship.tip: Confirm it is open before travelling to Bygdøy; the nearby Fram and Kon-Tiki museums are good backups.

munch.name: Munch Museum
munch.price_text: ≈ NOK 160–200 adult · check on the day
munch.tip: The Scream rooms are on an upper floor. Buy tickets online to skip the queue.

palace.name: The Royal Palace
palace.price_text: Palace tours have a fee · park free
palace.hours: Palace interior only in summer, guided tours · park open daily
palace.tip: The daily changing of the guard is around 13:30. Check the day and time before you go.

fram.name: Fram Museum
fram.price_text: ≈ NOK 140–180 adult · check on the day
fram.tip: You can walk inside the polar ship Fram. Allow time for the neighbouring Kon-Tiki Museum.

farikal.name: Fårikål
farikal.price_text: ≈ NOK 200–350 per main in a casual restaurant
farikal.hours: Served in autumn; many restaurants in September
farikal.tip: Fårikål is Norway's national dish: lamb and cabbage stew. Try it in late September when it is in season.

holmenkollen.name: Holmenkollen Ski Museum
holmenkollen.price_text: ≈ NOK 140–180 adult · ski jump tower included
holmenkollen.tip: Take metro line 1 to Holmenkollen. Climb the ski jump tower for the best view over Oslo.

kontiki.name: Kon-Tiki Museum
kontiki.price_text: ≈ NOK 120–160 adult · check on the day
kontiki.tip: See the original Kon-Tiki raft and the Ra II. Combine with the Fram Museum next door.

scream.name: The Scream
scream.price_text: Included in Munch Museum ticket, ≈ NOK 160–200
scream.tip: The painting is shown in a dedicated room. Go early to see it before tour groups arrive.

tusenfryd.name: TusenFryd
tusenfryd.price_text: ≈ NOK 450–600 day pass · check on the day
tusenfryd.tip: It is outside the city centre; check the bus or train route and opening dates before you go.

ullevaal.name: Ullevaal Stadion
ullevaal.price_text: Match tickets vary · check on the day
ullevaal.hours: Only on match days or tours
ullevaal.tip: This is Norway's national football stadium. Check the fixture list if you want a match.

mathallen.name: Mathallen Oslo food hall
mathallen.hours: Tue–Sat roughly 10:00–18:00/19:00 · Sun shorter · check on the day
mathallen.tip: Good stop for lunch in Grünerløkka. Try local cheese and smoked fish.

grunerlokka.name: Grünerløkka neighbourhood walk
grunerlokka.hours: Always open · cafés and shops daytime
grunerlokka.tip: Walk along the Akerselva river and the side streets for cafés, vintage shops and street art.

akerbrygge.name: Aker Brygge waterfront
akerbrygge.price_text: Free to walk · food and drinks extra
akerbrygge.tip: Walk the promenade from Aker Brygge to Tjuvholmen for fjord views and the Astrup Fearnley Museum.

fjordcruise.name: Oslofjord sightseeing boat
fjordcruise.price_text: ≈ NOK 300–500 for a short fjord cruise · check on the day
fjordcruise.tip: Boats leave near Rådhuset. Book a short cruise if you have limited time.

akerselva.name: Akerselva river walk
akerselva.tip: A green path with old mills and small waterfalls. Walk upstream from Grünerløkka.

karljohan.name: Karl Johans gate walk
karljohan.tip: The main street runs from Central Station to the Royal Palace. A simple orientation walk on day one.

sognsvann.name: Sognsvann lake
sognsvann.tip: Take metro line 5 to Sognsvann for a flat lakeside loop and forest paths.

stays.why: Walk to the Opera, Karl Johans gate and the palace; best transport links for day trips.
Waterfront dining and the ferry pier to Bygdøy museums and the islands.
Cafés, bars and a local feel along the Akerselva river; trams to the centre.
Quiet and central-west; close to Vigeland Park and the T-bane to Holmenkollen.

food: Try Norwegian basics: salmon, fish soup, kjøttkaker (meat cakes) and brown cheese on bread.
Lunch is the cheaper meal. Many restaurants serve the same dishes at lower midday prices.
Mathallen food hall at Vulkan has many small vendors; good for picky eaters and rainy days.
Seafood counters and the fish market area near the harbour are worth a look; check prices first, Norway is costly.
Tap water is safe and free. Alcohol is sold in state Vinmonopolet shops; bars are expensive.
more_time: Take a fjord ferry to the islands for a half-day of walking and swimming in summer.
Swap one museum for a forest walk or a trip up to Holmenkollen for views over the city.
